content:
Quick notes / scratchpad from loop (first pass for discussion)

High level takeaway: Sofia is a solid candidate for Senior ML Eng on serving runtime. Strong on systems design for inference, practical experience with KV caching and warm-start strategies, and good intuition about memory/throughput tradeoffs. Code exercise showed basic correctness but less polish on edge cases. I would lean hire if we get alignment on ownership and ability to productize her prototype ideas.

Panel notes (by interviewer):
- Jordan (runtime): really liked her proposed hybrid sharding idea (static + dynamic split) to handle hot prefixes. Follow-up: ask for latency tail analysis (p99) and how they'd instrument fallback to smaller model variants.
- Alex (infra): liked her approach to cache eviction (LRU + frequency heuristics) but concerned about lock contention at high concurrency. Suggested exploring lock-free ring buffers or sharded locks - Sofia was aware and had implemented sharded locks in previous role but didn't detail tradeoffs.
- Priya (coding): implementation correct but didn't account for worst-case sequence length blowup in complexity. Missed small optimization: reusing KV cache allocations across batches.
- Hiring mgr (brief): wants someone who can push optimizations into prod quickly; Sofia has prior on-call for inference infra and is comfortable with hotfixes.

Strengths:
- Practical systems experience: has shipped inference optimizations (quantization + cache) in production at mid-size startup.
- Good communicator: breaks down tradeoffs clearly and is collaborative.
- Ownership: described owning a rollout from prototype to canary to full deploy.

Concerns / Areas to probe in follow-up:
- Coding thoroughness: needs to show more attention to edge cases and complexity; ask for a follow-up small take-home to see code quality and tests.
- Scalability under extreme tail (p99): want concrete instrumentation and mitigation plan for p99 spikes (circuit breakers, backpressure).
- Prioritization/product sense: her prioritization rationale is more engineering-first; check alignment with product tradeoffs (cost vs latency).

Suggested next steps:
- Call with hiring manager for 30m to discuss production rollout examples and p99 mitigation in depth. (Action: Jordan to set up)
- Optional take-home: small coding + test exercise focused on cache reuse and edge-case handling (2-3 hours). (Action: Priya to draft prompt)
- Check references for delivery speed and post-deploy incident handling.

Slack notes / quick quote to include in loop summary: "Strong systems person, productizable ideas, coding needs polish. Lean hire if references + follow-up coding are clean."

Open questions (to include in final ballot):
- How did the quantization changes affect downstream quality/regressions in their product? Any A/B results?
- Exact tenure owning the inference infra: single contributor vs team lead?
- On-call experience: frequency and typical incident types handled.

Draft ballot language (short): "Sofia demonstrated strong systems design and production inference experience. She communicates tradeoffs well and has shipped relevant features; coding exercise revealed correct approach but needs more rigor on edge cases. Recommend move to hiring manager call + optional coding take-home; overall lean hire pending references and coding follow-up."

Notes to self: include JIRA loop ticket JIRA-4567 and attach code snippet from live exercise (Jordan captured in GH gist) before sending to hiring manager.

-- Priya (notes)
